Mosquitoes become infectious day \(\tau+1.\) \[Y_{+1, t+1} = p \left(1-G_i \right) Y_{, t} \] \[Y_{\tau, t+1} = p \left(1-G_{\tau-1} \right) Y_{\tau-1, t} + p \left(1-G_\tau \right) Y_{\tau, t}\] \(Z_t\) denote density infectious mosquitoes time \(t\) \[Z_{t+1} = \sum_i p G_i Y_i  + p Z_t\] defined variables, one necessary, since \[U = M- \sum_i Y_i - Z\]

title: Macdonald's Model
text: Macdonald’s model sporozoite rate, published 19521 played important role studies malaria. Later year, Macdonald introduced formula basic reproductive rate, now called \(R_0.\)2 Macdonald gives credit colleague Armitage mathematics. Armitage’s paper published next year,3 paper present model system differential equations. simple system differential equations consistent Macdonald’s model sporozoite rate three parameters one term: human blood feeding rate, \(\) extrinsic incubation period, \(\tau\) mosquito death rate, \(g\); probability surviving one day, \(p=e^{-g}\), \(g=-\ln p\) fraction bites humans infect mosquito, \(\kappa\) Let \(y\) denote fraction mosquitoes infected. dynamics given : \[\frac{dy}{dt} = \kappa (1-y) - g y\] Let \(z\) denote fraction mosquitoes infectious. model delay differential equation. Let \(y_\tau\) denote value \(y\) time \(t-\tau.\) parameters terms constant, :\[\frac{dz}{dt} = e^{-g\tau} \kappa (1-y_\tau) - g z\] model steady state fraction infected: \[\bar y = \frac{\kappa} {\kappa + g}\] fraction infectious, also called sporozoite rate, \[\bar z = \frac{\kappa} {\kappa + g}e^{-g\tau}.\] Macdonald used \(p\) formula : \[\bar z = \frac{\kappa} {\kappa -\ln p}e^{-p\tau}\] generate formula \(R_0,\) Macdonald introduces another variable three additional parameters: ratio mosquitoes humans, \(m\) rate infections clear, \(r\) fraction infectious bites infect human, \(b\) fraction infected infectious humans, \(x,\) given equation: \[\frac{dx}{dt} = m z (1-y) - r x\] model assumes \(\kappa = x.\) formula \(R_0\) system : \[R_0 = \frac{m b ^2}{gr} e^{-g\tau} = \frac{m b ^2}{(-\ln p)r} e^{-p\tau}\] form, model difficult use extend.

title: Macdonald's Model
text: mosquito module ramp.xds called macdonald based model first published 1982 Joan Aron Robert May4. includes state variables total mosquito density \(M\), infected mosquito density \(Y\), infectious mosquito density \(Z\). model, blood feeding rate split overall blood feeding rate, \(f\), human fraction, \(q\) \[=fq.\] Aron & May’s equations : \[\begin{array}{rl} \frac{dM}{dt} &= \Lambda(t) - g M \\ \frac{dY}{dt} &= fq\kappa(M-Y) - g Y \\ \frac{dZ}{dt} &= e^{-g\tau}fq\kappa_\tau(M_\tau-Y_\tau) - g Z \\ \end{array}\]

code: nStrata <- 3 H <- c(100, 500, 250) residence = rep(1,3) membership=1 xds_obj <- make_xds_object_template("xde", "eir", 1, membership, residence) b <- 0.55 c1 <- 0.05 c2 <- 0.25 r1 <- 1/250 r2 <- 1/50 m2 <- rlnorm(3, .2, .5)  h <- r2*m2 m1 <- h/r1 Xo = list(b = b, c1 = c1, c2 = c2, r1 = r1, r2 = r2, m1=m1, m2=m2, H=H) eir <- h/b xds_obj = setup_XH_obj("hMoI", residence, xds_obj, options=Xo, i=1) xds_obj = setup_MY_obj("trivialMY", xds_obj, s=1) xds_obj = setup_L_obj("trivialL", 1, xds_obj, s=1) F_season = F_one F_trend = F_one F_shock = F_one xds_obj$EIR_obj = list()  xds_obj$EIR_obj$eir <- as.vector(eir) xds_obj$EIR_obj$scale <- 1  xds_obj$EIR_obj$F_season <- F_season xds_obj$EIR_obj$F_trend <- F_trend xds_obj$EIR_obj$F_shock <- F_shock xds_obj$EIR_obj$F_age <- F_one xds_obj$EIR_obj$season_par <- list()  xds_obj$EIR_obj$trend_par<- list()  xds_obj$EIR_obj$shock_par<- list()  xds_obj$EIR_obj$age_par<- list()  xds_obj$EIR_obj$bday <-0 xds_obj = make_indices(xds_obj) y0 <- get_inits(xds_obj) y0 #> $L #> list() #>  #> $MY #> NULL #>  #> $X #> $X$m1 #> [1] 3.032587 6.938575 1.805443 #>  #> $X$m2 #> [1] 0.6065175 1.3877150 0.3610886 #>  #>  #> $V #> NULL xds_obj <- xds_solve(xds_obj)  XH <- xds_obj$outputs$orbits$XH[[1]] time <- xds_obj$outputs$time clrs = turbo(5) plot(time, XH$m1[,1], col = clrs[1], ylim = range(XH$m1), type = "l") lines(time, XH$m1[,2], col = clrs[2]) lines(time, XH$m1[,3], col =clrs[5])    lines(time, XH$m2[,1], col = clrs[1], lty = 2) lines(time, XH$m2[,2], col = clrs[2], lty=2) lines(time, XH$m2[,3], col =clrs[5], lty=2)

text: discrete-time system, demographic change \(I_t\) computed two steps: survival \((I_s)\) infection dynamics: \[ \begin{array}{rcc} & \mathbf{X} & \mathbf{H} \\ \hline H_{t+1} =& &B(t,H_t) - \mathbf{D}(t,H_t)\\ I_s  =& & I_t -  \mathbf{D}(t,I_t) \\   I_{t+1} &= \alpha_t(1-\rho) (H_{t+1} + I_s) + e^{-\left(r + h\rho + \sigma + \Xi \left( t \right) \right)} I_s \\ \end{array} \]

text: Blood feeding modeled interaction hosts spend time patches mosquitoes search blood hosts. host population stratum per-capita search weight \((w)\). fraction time spent outside patches time away \((\delta)\) (see time_away), population density present spatial domain \((1-\delta)H\). time-spent matrix \((\Theta)\) describes hosts allocate time among patches. Ambient host population density patch $$= \Theta \cdot ((1-\delta)H),$$ vector multiplication element-wise. time--risk matrix \((\Psi)\) weights time spent relative mosquito activity day (see time_at_risk). Human availability patches $$W = \Psi \cdot (w(1-\delta)H),$$ product inside parentheses element-wise. Search weights specific host species shared across vector species. Availability can differ vector species can different time--risk matrix.

what: The GeM module for the MY component — GeM
title: The GeM module for the MY component — GeM
text: GeM generalized, non-autonomous Macdonald model mosquito ecology infection dynamics. includes adult mosquito density emergence, spatial dynamics, time-varying survival dispersal potentially time-varying extrinsic incubation period (EIP).

title: The GeM module for the MY component — GeM
text: M density adult mosquitoes P density parous adult mosquitoes Y density infected adult mosquitoes Z density infectious adult mosquitoes

title: The GeM module for the MY component — GeM
text: Lambda \(\Lambda\) adult mosquito emergence rate, computed Emergence kappa \(\kappa\) net infectiousness, computed Transmission

title: The GeM module for the MY component — GeM
text: f blood feeding rate — use setup_f setup_blood_feeding_rates q human fraction — use setup_q setup_human_fractions g mosquito mortality rate — use setup_g setup_mosquito_mortality eip \(\tau\) extrinsic incubation period — use setup_eip sigma \(\sigma\) emigration rate — use setup_sigma setup_mosy_emigration mu \(\mu\) emigration loss fraction — use setup_mu setup_emigration_loss K K_matrix mosquito dispersal matrix — use setup_K_matrix nu \(\nu\) oviposition rate: number egg batches laid patch, per mosquito, per day — use setup_nu setup_egg_batch_rates eggs_per_batch number eggs per batch basic setup, change_MY_pars.GeM can used change static parameter values. default, bionomic parameters configured static baselines; advanced setup can used define dynamic ports.

title: The GeM module for the MY component — GeM
text: Mosquito survival dispersal described demographic matrix \(\Omega(t)\): $$\Omega(t)=\mbox{diag}(g(t)+\sigma(t)\mu(t))-K\cdot\mbox{diag}(\sigma(t)(1-\mu(t))).$$ parameter \(g\) per-capita mortality rate mosquitoes patch. Mosquitoes emigrate patches per-capita rates \(\sigma\), fraction \(\mu\) emigrating mosquitoes lost. columns dispersal matrix \(K\) sum zero. non-trivial dispersal matrices, \(\mbox{diag}(K)=-1\); -diagonal elements describe fractions surviving emigrants arrive patches.

title: The GeM module for the MY component — GeM
text: Let \(\tau(t)\) EIP mosquito infected time \(t\); becomes infectious time \(t+\tau(t)\). Let \(\tau'(t)\) elapsed time since infection mosquito becomes infectious time \(t\). quantities satisfy $$\tau(t)=\tau'(t+\tau(t)) \qquad \tau'(t)=\tau(t-\tau'(t)).$$ F_eip function returns lag \(\tau'(t)\) used delay equations. time-varying EIP also requires derivative, computed dF_eip.

title: The GeM module for the MY component — GeM
text: matrix \(\Upsilon(t)\) represents survival dispersal time-varying EIP, \(t_\tau=t-\tau'(t)\) \(t\). autonomous case \(e^{-\Omega\tau}\). time-varying demography EIP, computed accessory variable: $$\frac{d\Upsilon}{dt}=\left(\Omega(t_\tau)\left(1-\frac{d\tau'(t)}{dt}\right)-\Omega(t)\right)\cdot\Upsilon(t).$$ initial matrix set \(\exp(-\Omega eip)\). variable internal model output orbit.

title: The GeM module for the MY component — GeM
text: ML interface supplies Lambda \(\Lambda\), adult mosquito emergence rate, using outputs L component. XY interface supplies kappa \(\kappa\), net infectiousness, using outputs XH component.

title: The GeM module for the MY component — GeM
text: subscript \(\tau\) denotes value parameter, term, variable time \(t-\tau'(t)\): $$X_\tau=X(t-\tau'(t)).$$ derivatives state variables : $$ \begin{array}{rl} dM/dt &= \Lambda-\Omega\cdot M \\\\ dP/dt &= f(M-P)-\Omega\cdot P \\\\ dY/dt &= fq\kappa(M-Y)-\Omega\cdot Y \\\\ dZ/dt &= \Upsilon\cdot(fq\kappa)_\tau(M_\tau-Y_\tau)-\Omega\cdot Z \end{array}$$ implementation also evolves \(\Upsilon\) accessory variables used evaluate delayed values \(fq\kappa\), \(g\), \(\sigma\).

title: The GeM module for the MY component — GeM
text: oviposition rate \(\nu\) number eggs per batch, eggs_per_batch, determine egg production rate per patch: $$G=\nu M\cdot\texttt{eggs\_per\_batch}.$$ F_eggs.GeM computes \(G\), passed EggLaying distribution among aquatic habitats.

title: The GeM module for the MY component — GeM
text: human biting density, fqM, number human bites per patch per day; infective biting density, fqZ, number infectious human bites per patch per day. F_fqM.GeM F_fqZ.GeM compute quantities \(f q M\) \(f q Z\), respectively. compute_EIR combines infective biting density biting distribution matrix resident-bite fraction compute stratum-level EIR. F_hbr uses fqM, matrix, resident-bite fraction compute stratum-level HBR.

title: The GeM module for the MY component — GeM
text: Macdonald G (1952) analysis sporozoite rate. Tropical Diseases Bulletin 49:569-586. Aron JL, May RM (1982) population dynamics malaria. Chapter 5 Population Dynamics Infectious Diseases: Theory Applications, Springer, Boston, MA. Wu SL, et al. (2023) Spatial dynamics malaria transmission. PLoS Computational Biology 19(6): e1010684. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010684

text: Update state variables RMdts module: $$\begin{array}{rl} M_t &= \Lambda+\Omega\cdot M_{t-1} \\\\ P_t &= f(M_{t-1}-P_{t-1})+\Omega\cdot P_{t-1} \\\\ U_t &= \Lambda+\Omega\cdot(e^{-fq\kappa}U_{t-1}) \\\\ \widetilde{Y}_t &= \Omega\cdot\left(Y_{t-1}\cdot\operatorname{diag}(1-G_t)\right) \\\\ Z_t &= \Omega\cdot(Y_{t-1}\cdot G_t)+\Omega\cdot Z_{t-1} \end{array}$$ G_t G[Gix], Gix = c(t-1:max_eip) %% max_eip + 1. Let \(\) eip_day_ix = (t %% max_eip) + 1 \(b\) eip_yday_ix = ((t-1) %% max_eip) + 1. Starting \(Y_t=\widetilde{Y}_t\), apply column assignments order: $$\begin{array}{rl} Y_t[,b] &\leftarrow Y_t[,b]+Y_t[,] \\\\ Y_t[,] &\leftarrow \Omega\cdot\left((1-e^{-fq\kappa})U_{t-1}\right) \end{array}$$

Hosts Traps — Local hosts compete visitors, blood hosts, blood traps mosquito blood-seeking activity: \(W\) — local host availability \(V\) — visitor availability \(O\) — blood host availability \(T\) — blood trap availability $$B = W + V + O + T$$ Mosquito Bionomics — Blood-feeding rates mosquito bionomic parameters can modeled functional responses availability. example: $$f = F_f(B, \ldots)$$ positive total availability, availability-based host fraction : $$q = \frac{W+V}{B}$$ modeling relationship, constraint automatically imposed every module. Directly assigned bionomic parameters need satisfy . Bites Local Hosts — local fraction separates bites local hosts bites visitors: $$\ell = \frac{W}{W+V}$$ F_local_frac sets fraction one \(W+V=0\). single vector species, human/host biting rate daily local EIR computed using mixing_matrix: $$\mbox{HBR} = \beta \cdot (\ell f q M)$$ $$\mbox{EIR} = \beta \cdot (\ell f q Z)$$ Products within parentheses element-wise. multiple vector species, contributions summed host stratum. transmission interface also computes net infectiousness mosquitoes. text: Mosquito survival dispersal described demographic matrix \(\Omega\). parameter \(g\) per-capita mortality rate mosquitoes patch. Mosquitoes emigrate patches per-capita rates \(\sigma\), fraction \(\mu\) emigrating mosquitoes lost. combined rate mortality loss emigration $$g+\mu\sigma.$$ columns mosquito dispersal matrix \(K\) sum zero. non-trivial dispersal matrices, \(\mbox{diag}(K)=-1\); -diagonal elements describe fractions surviving emigrants arrive patches. demographic matrix $$\Omega=\mbox{diag}(g+\sigma\mu)-K\cdot\mbox{diag}(\sigma(1-\mu)).$$ Survival dispersal EIP represented $$\Upsilon=e^{-\Omega\tau}.$$

F_beta replaces zero entries \(W\) one dividing, avoid division zero. one host species, fraction bites local hosts patch \(j\) received stratum \(\) \(H_i \beta_{,j}\). entries \(\beta\) alone per-capita allocation weights, fractions bites. \(D\) mosquito biting density patch \(\ell\) local fraction, biting rate stratum : $$\beta \cdot (\ell D)$$ product \(\ell D\) element-wise. title: Set up the module object for GeM (MY) — setup_MY_obj.GeM
text: Let \(\tau(t)\) EIP mosquito infected time \(t\); becomes infectious time \(t+\tau(t)\). Let \(\tau'(t)\) elapsed time since infection mosquito becomes infectious time \(t\). quantities satisfy $$\tau(t)=\tau'(t+\tau(t)) \qquad \tau'(t)=\tau(t-\tau'(t)).$$ F_eip function returns lag \(\tau'(t)\) used delay equations. time-varying EIP also requires derivative, computed dF_eip.

title: Set up the module object for GeM (MY) — setup_MY_obj.GeM
text: matrix \(\Upsilon(t)\) represents survival dispersal time-varying EIP, \(t_\tau=t-\tau'(t)\) \(t\). autonomous case \(e^{-\Omega\tau}\). time-varying demography EIP, computed accessory variable: $$\frac{d\Upsilon}{dt}=\left(\Omega(t_\tau)\left(1-\frac{d\tau'(t)}{dt}\right)-\Omega(t)\right)\cdot\Upsilon(t).$$ initial matrix set \(\exp(-\Omega eip)\). variable internal model output orbit.

text: Patch spatial unit adult mosquito populations interactions resources represented. See xds_info_patch_dynamics. See xds_info_aquatic_habitats. Residence patch population stratum lives, need patch spends time. See residence_vector. Residence matrix matrix aggregates quantities population strata patch residence. See residence_matrix. Habitat Membership patch location assigned aquatic habitat. See habitat_vector. Habitat matrix matrix aggregates quantities aquatic habitats patch. See habitat_matrix.

title: Glossary for ramp.xds — xds_glossary
text: Search weight weight assigned host stratum habitat contributes availability searching mosquitoes. See xds_info_search_weights. Availability measure accessibility mosquitoes, rather abundance alone, incorporates search weights , hosts, time risk. See available_blood_hosts habitat_availability. Blood feeding interaction mosquitoes searching blood hosts hosts spending time patches. See blood_feeding. Egg laying allocation eggs laid adult mosquitoes patches among aquatic habitats. See egg_laying. Laying matrix matrix distributes eggs patches aquatic habitats according relative availability. See laying_matrix. Emergence transition aquatic immature stages adult mosquitoes patches. See xds_info_emergence. Bionomics demographic behavioral properties mosquitoes, including feeding, survival, movement, development. See xds_info_mosquito_bionomics. Functional response relationship expresses mosquito bionomic parameter function resource availability. See blood_feeding.

title: Glossary for ramp.xds — xds_glossary
text: Time spent fraction time population stratum spends patch traveling. See xds_info_time_spent. Time risk Time spent traveling, weighted mosquito activity. See time_at_risk. Time away fraction time spent outside spatial domain represented patches. See xds_port_time_away. Travel malaria Exposure malaria outside modeled spatial domain. See xds_info_travel_malaria. Visitor non-resident host whose availability infectiousness contribute blood feeding transmission patches. See xds_info_visitors. Local fraction fraction blood feeding local hosts among blood meals local hosts visitors. See xds_info_local_fraction. Environmental heterogeneity Variation exposure within population stratum, represented model distribution bites. See xds_info_environmental_heterogeneity. Relative biting rate stratum's daily EIR relative population average daily EIR. See xds_info_relative_biting_rates.

title: Glossary for ramp.xds — xds_glossary
text: Mixing matrix biting distribution matrix maps biting density patches per-capita biting rates population strata. See mixing_matrix. HBR Human/host biting rate: number mosquito bites per person host per day. See F_hbr. EIR Entomological inoculation rate: number infective bites per person host per day. See F_eir xds_info_transmission. FoI Force infection: rate acquiring infection. See F_foi xds_info_exposure. Attack rate probability acquiring infection time step. See F_ar Exposure. Infected mosquito mosquito carrying infection, need yet capable transmitting . See MY_module_list. Infective mosquito mosquito capable transmitting pathogen bite. See F_fqZ. Infectivity probability host infection per infective bite, potentially affected immunity. See F_infectivity. Infectiousness capacity infected host population infect mosquitoes blood feeding. See F_I. Net infectiousness probability mosquito becomes infected feeding modeled hosts visitors patch. See F_kappa xds_info_transmission.

title: Solve Cohort Dynamics — xds_solve_cohort
text: Given forcing function describing average EIR population time, simulate malaria cohort ages, using age independent variable \(()\) rather time \((t)\). Relative biting rates age set \(F_\omega()\) F_age associated parameters age_par. solve, argument birthday sets birthday cohort, \((d)\). user either passes ages Amax da configure vector ages output wanted \((a_i)\), times \(t_i=a_i+d\). effect, since \(= t-d\), function solves system exposure function pattern: $$F_\omega() \times F_S(t-d) \times F_T(t-d) \times F_K(t-d)$$
